channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Politico Europe] Iran denies role in cyberattacks on French supermarket refrigerators
item.description: Paris pointed the finger at Tehran for the attacks on Monday.

item.title: [Financial Times] Top Federal Reserve official considers largest rate rise since 2022
item.description: Governor Christopher Waller says policymakers should weigh a 50-basis-point move if US inflation fails to slow

item.title: [EU Observer] Digital Fairness Act: EU cracks down on stealth influencer ads and manipulative app design
item.description: The Digital Fairness Act aims to impose stricter protections for people online. While the leaked draft proposes to ban overly-complicated choices to refuse data-sharing, it does not ban addictive design practises outright, warns rights watchdog EDRi. Meanwhile, online retailer Omio have complained that compliance will be costly to businesses.

item.description: Quantum Systems teamed up with UFORCE to secure the first term as co-chair

item.description: Figure of 0.4% comes as last year’s government shutdown prevented data collection

item.title: [Euractiv] Climate action and health resilience are ‘investments in the same thing’, experts say [Partner Content]
item.description: Health systems must protect patients from climate impacts while cutting their own emissions. Experts at the World Health Summit in Berlin said the two tasks reinforce each other, and that prevention serves both.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU needs only ‘very trusted partners’ on AI chips, tech chief says amid Nvidia crisis
item.description: “We want to really keep the business secrets in Europe,” Henna Virkkunen says about EU efforts to protect sensitive industries.

item.title: [EU Observer] As many Russians killed near Pokrovsk in Ukraine as Soviet troops killed in the 1945 Battle of Berlin, according to hacked data (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,720)
item.description: The data leak reveals a war so costly that battles around Pokrovsk now rival some of the most arrowing clashes of WW2, potentially reshaping how Moscow and Kyiv — as well as their allies — calculate their next moves on the front.

item.title: [Financial Times] Goldman Sachs expects Anthropic revenue to exceed $600bn by 2030
item.description: Wall Street bank projects AI start-up will increase sales by 130 times — and be cash flow positive — by end of the decade

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Commission to host security talks after week of bomb hoaxes that hit 20 airports and dozens of European flights
item.description: Experts from EU member states will meet on Wednesday to discuss last week’s bomb hoaxes affecting dozens of flights across Europe and causing millions in losses.

item.description: The Slovak prime minister lambasted the German chancellor's proposal as "blackmail."

item.title: [EU Observer] The Kraków shooting: A Polish tragedy, a Russian opportunity
item.description: As soon as a few images of the perpetrator and the contents of the boot of his car appeared in the media, the Russian propaganda machine was set to work.

item.description: Any EU envoy for peace talks with Russia should meet four criteria, the Russian ex-spy said: no border with Russia, no conflicts of interest, no fear of Donald Trump, and willingness to "bloody" Vladimir Putin's nose.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU-backed Black Sea security hub to become operational in 2027
item.description: Bucharest and Sofia are negotiating a memorandum of understanding to operationalise the Hub

item.title: [Euractiv] Transport Policy Conference 2026
item.description: The EU’s push to decarbonise transport is accelerating, with new rules on CO2 standards, clean fuels, batteries, and infrastructure set to reshape the sector in the coming years.

item.description: Draft text aims to dial up platforms' response to political deepfakes

item.title: [Euractiv] EU’s defence future: integrated market, stronger eastern flank and Ukraine at its core [Promoted Content]
item.description: Europe has ambitious defence plans and budgets are rising. But genuine readiness will depend on whether it can build an integrated defence market, accelerate industrial production and place its eastern Member States and Ukraine at the heart of the transformation.

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs pick apart Commission’s data centre sustainability scheme

item.description: The Abu Dhabi meetings open with an agreement between the U.S. and EU to look at a new security structure for Europe when Russia's war on Ukraine ends.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
item.description: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

item.title: [Politico Europe] US military aircraft pulled from second UK base after ‘Iran threat’
item.description: Bombers were withdrawn from RAF Fairford in October after an Iran-linked security incident.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Prince Harry slams ‘lawless’ social media’s impact on children
item.description: Duke and Duchess of Sussex visit the European Parliament.

item.title: [Euractiv] Car data rights exist on paper. Now they need to work in practice [Promoted Content]
item.description: A new study prepared for FIA Region I finds that while the Data Act gives vehicle users the right to access and share data generated by their cars, the revised Annex X to the Type-Approval Regulation establishes technical requirements for independent operators to access vehicle repair and maintenance information. However, meaningful access still depends on fair pricing, consistency and effective consent mechanisms. Rights on paper are only a first step.

item.description: Maltese finance minister Clyde Caruana said Malta "supports the objectives" of the reform, but said that the "proposed minimum [excise tax] rates remain well above current national levels."

item.description: Diplomats say the bloc has reached a consensus to support the summit's keynote pledge.

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
item.description: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

item.description: Talks on peace in Ukraine are set to continue this week in Abu Dhabi. And this time, the EU appears to have found a way into the room. But what can actually be expected from these negotiations?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Is Burnham’s No 10 North working out?
item.description: Is the battle over welfare reforms about to intensify? With the Milburn Report on youth unemployment just a week away, Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy examine the growing pressure on Labour to tackle the issue. And with the head of the civil service, Antonia Romeo, preparing Whitehall for a spending squeeze, the Conservatives are planning […]

item.title: [DW] US, Russia and Ukraine start talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US are getting underway in the United Arab Emirates. It is the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Investigation] Thousands deported with Frontex help never see promised EU reintegration money
item.description: Internal minutes show Frontex urging national authorities and NGOs to run sensitive data past the agency before talking to journalists, even as it insists “transparency is the rule” and refuses to release basic figures on who actually got paid.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Can the EU’s climate strategy survive election season?
item.description: The EU wants to be a heavyweight at U.N. climate summits. But upcoming elections across the bloc could upend those efforts. As COP31 kicks off this week, Zoya Sheftalovich and Ian Wishart discuss how the populist surge across the continent could undermine the EU’s efforts to take a stronger leadership role in climate talks like […]

item.title: [Financial Times] VW pivots again as ‘In China, For China’ runs out of road
item.description: The German group is changing its strategy in the world’s largest car market as it struggles with a sharp downturn

item.title: [Financial Times] The last of the Botíns
item.description: The Santander chief says she will be the last in her family to run the bank

item.title: [Financial Times] Investors pile into defensive stocks amid fears AI bull market may be over
item.description: Consumer staples and healthcare among sectors to perform strongly as investors fret over future tech earnings

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump says FBI is ‘looking into’ Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
item.description: US company has been rocked by allegations its chief executive had an affair with a Chinese spy

item.title: [DW] Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins postelection cleanup
item.description: The landslide victory of the Student List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

item.title: [DW] Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
item.description: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

item.title: [DW] Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
item.description: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

item.title: [DW] Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
item.description: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

item.title: [DW] Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
item.description: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
item.description: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: [DW] Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
item.description: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

item.title: [DW] New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
item.description: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

item.title: [DW] Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
item.description: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

item.title: [DW] EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
item.description: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.

item.title: [DW] Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
item.description: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.

item.title: [EU Observer] €120m in totally unused border facilities is the latest bill for the monumental waste that was Brexit
item.description: Hundreds of millions have been wasted on Brexit border checks that either don't work or were never used. It's a fitting monument to a failure to plan.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia’s ‘key man’ risk
item.description: Some of the leading AI companies are dangerously reliant on single executives

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs demand Belgium evacuate visa-holders from Gaza as winter flooding makes life catastrophic
item.description: 1,800 people hold Belgian visas for family reunifications or university studies, yet remain stuck in Gaza. And while EU officials and Belgian authorities pass accountability back and forth, devastating floods have displaced even more already displaced people - and a handful of MEPs stand up for the Palestinians that will have to suffer another winter outdoors.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia goes quiet on claims of territorial wins, starts bragging about air-strikes on Ukrainian cities instead (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,719)
item.description: Russian Z-channels have stopped reporting on movements along the contact lines, instead publishing lists of cities struck by Russian drones and missiles.

item.title: [EU Observer] Fake bomb warnings are hitting European aviation – but the bigger threat came from Jared Kushner
item.description: Every one of the 70-plus warnings sent to airlines, newsrooms and other targets in Europe last week was a hoax. But the harm was real: planes diverted, buildings evacuated, plans disrupted, costs incurred, public confidence eroded, writes Edward Lucas.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Whenever we take pro-European political decisions, Russia cut or reduced gas supplies’. Moldova energy minister Dorin Junghietu on why Chișinău is betting on diversification
item.description: Moldova suffers from soaring blackout costs and fragile Soviet-era lines. Chisinau, in response, on Monday, inaugurated a new electric grid, linking to Romania and the European grid. The country's energy minister tells EUobserver: 'Russia uses energy as a weapon, and they did it also to Moldova. Whenever we tried to take pro-European political decisions, Russia cut or reduced gas supplies.'

item.title: [EU Observer] Israel’s anti-Netanyahu bloc needs Europe’s help to stabilise Middle East
item.description: The recent elections in Israel and the US create a narrow geopolitical opening for de-escalation in the Middle East, which Europe should seize upon instead of playing wait and see.

item.title: [EU Observer] The clock is ticking: Europe is running out of time to save the International Criminal Court
item.description: The US midterms have opened a political window for Europe. With a key US licence expiring in April 2027, Brussels must turn its rhetorical support for the ICC into concrete action before this opportunity closes.

item.title: [DW] Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
item.description: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.
